newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs rise on position adjustment, cash-bond buying.
newsitem.headline: JGBs rise on position adjustment, cash-bond buying.

text.p: The key December Japanese government bond futures ended higher on Friday, due to position adjustment ahead of the weekend and buying of cash JGBs by investors.
Traders said investors were said to have bought long-term cash JGBs.
"Investors are said to have bought cash JGBs between the 180th and 189th issues," a trader at a city bank's securities affiliate said.
A trader for a regional bank said pension funds were said to have bought cash JGBs during the morning session.
The December ended at 124.70, up from Thursday's 124.45.
Traders said the December is expected to be supported on the downside as a shift in benchmark status to the March JGB futures contract is expected later this month.
"Before the change in the benchmark, the December might test 125.00," said a trader at a brokerage house.

During the morning session, a vague rumour that the Bank of Japan might tighten its monetary policy circulated in the market and drove the December down to an intraday low of 124.20, but it rebounded from there soon after, traders said.
An investment fund set up as part of a government scheme to solve the financial problems of failed mortgage companies has invested in Treasury Bills (T-bills) recently, market sources said.

The New Financial Stabilisation Fund, which was set up as part of a government scheme to solve the financial problems of failed mortgage companies, is said to have bought an estimated 200 billion to 300 billion yen worth of T-bills, a trust bank trader said.
The trader said there were rumours the Fund may buy the T-bills which were offered through on auction on Friday.
The Finance Ministry (MOF) offered 1.5 trillion yen worth of three-month T-bills through a price competitive auction on Friday.
The lowest price and the average price of the T-bills was 99.910 yen, MOF said.
Traders said the Fund was investing in short-term instruments for the time being, as the current level of long-term interest rates was too low.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.625 percent as of 0716 GMT, down from Thursday's 2.665 percent.
